gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ something to eat at the motorway services.
gaps.explanation: 'Stopped to get' = paused for the purpose; 'stopped getting' would mean quit eating.

gaps.sentence: Remember ___ your passport to the airport.
gaps.explanation: remember + to-infinitive = not forget to do something.

gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)

gaps.sentence: I resent ___ treated as an amateur when I have twenty years’ experience.
gaps.explanation: 'Resent' takes a gerund; the passive is 'being treated'.

gaps.sentence: We spent the whole morning ___ for tickets.
gaps.explanation: spend time + -ing: spent the morning queueing.

gaps.sentence: I saw him ___ the wall and disappear into the garden.
gaps.explanation: see/hear + object + bare infinitive = the complete action; -ing = the action in progress. Both readings possible here; the bare infinitive is expected.
